title: Searching grammar derivations
description: You can follow a bounded breadth-first search through arithmetic expressions.

steps.description: GRAMMAR maps each nonterminal to its possible replacements. You start the search with the single symbol E in both frontier and visited.
Each pass builds the next frontier. A completed terminal string is compared with target; otherwise the first nonterminal is replaced by each of its alternatives.

steps.question: Which part of candidate does the prefix check compare with target?
steps.answer: It compares only the terminals before the first remaining nonterminal. Those symbols have settled under leftmost expansion.

steps.description: You keep unseen candidates within the length bound and search for at most max_steps passes. The function returns False when those passes finish without a match.
The supplied output marks 2+3, 2*3, 1+2*3 and 9*8*7 True. You see False for 2++3, 2+ and +2.
